description.content:
Search

**Required Role:** Authenticated User with Active Organization

query.description: A comma separated list of collection GUIDs. The search results will only contain items from any of the given collections.

When set to true, if the search term refers to a custom attribute name or value, then the results will contain all items that have that custom attribute. For example, if the search term contains `business` then it gets all items with a custom attribute named `business` or with a custom attribute with a value containing the word `business`.
A comma separated list of data source types. The search results will only contain items from any of the given data source types.
A comma separated list of dbt tag GUIDs. The search results will only contain items tagged by any of the given tags.
A comma separated list of GUIDs to search for. When provided, other search parameters cannot be specified.

A comma separated list of object types to filter on. If specified, the search results will only contain objects whose types are specified. For example, if the filter is `include=tables,databases` then the search results will only contain tables and databases.
When set to true, exact matching will be turned off when no_fuzzy=false, and all search results will match the search terms fuzzily. No effect if no_fuzzy=true.
When set to true, fuzzy search won't be used. All search results will match the search terms exactly
When set to true, popularity won't be returned

Specify the ordering for the results. 

 A comma separated list for ordering by multiple fields and a preceding `-` indicates reverse order. 

Note: Order is case-sensitive.
A page number within the paginated result set.
Number of results to return per page.
An inclusive range of values that popularity must fall between. The syntax of this query must match the following regex: `\d{3}-\d{3}`
A comma separated list of status tag GUIDs. The search results will only contain items tagged by any of the given tags.

When set to true, if the search term refers to a tag name, then the results will contain all items that are tagged with that tag. For example, if the search term contains `pii` and `tags_search` is enabled, then the results will contain all items that tagged as `pii`
